parsed.title: TCP and UDP Protocols
summary_points: TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that uses a three-way handshake and guarantees reliable, in-order delivery.
TCP provides flow control via sliding window and congestion control, and is used for HTTP, email, and FTP.
UDP is connectionless, has no handshake, and offers no delivery or order guarantees.
UDP features a small 8-byte header and lower latency, making it faster than TCP.
UDP is used for DNS, video streaming, gaming, and VoIP where speed beats reliability.
parsed.one_line: TCP prioritizes reliable, ordered delivery, whereas UDP prioritizes speed and lower latency.
